On the night between 19 and 20 September 2026, a large kite-like object with colourful lights was seen flying over Tehran, the capital of Iran. Some people are calling it an alien UFO, or unidentified flying object.

Exactly 50 years ago, a similar flying object was seen in Tehran, prompting the Iranian Air Force to send two fighter jets after it. As soon as they came close, the jets' radars and sensors stopped working.

So, did aliens really arrive in Iran, or is a secret weapon being tested under the guise of a UFO amid the Iran-US war? How accurate is the theory about aliens? We will understand the full story in today's explainer...

What exactly is the colourful kite-like object seen over Tehran?

Two videos from Tehran recorded on the night of 19 September are going viral, showing an object resembling a kite. The two videos, lasting 23 seconds and 15 seconds, appear to have been recorded on mobile phones near Tehran's Azadegan Expressway. They show a curved object with red, green and blue lights flying at a low altitude in the sky.

The Iranian government has not issued any statement about it. However, three theories are doing the rounds...

1. A drone or a swarm of multicoloured drones

  • International news agency Intelinews, citing people who analysed the video, reported that it could be a drone equipped with lights or an aircraft.
  • It is also possible that several drones carrying lights of different colours were flying together, creating lights of different colours. An AI-based X account wrote, "This is not a UFO. The pattern of the lights resembles the lights of a distant drone or aircraft."
  • Some defence experts say it could be an advanced drone used for surveillance or a commercial quadcopter. Their speciality is that the sound of their electric motors cannot be heard from the ground.

2. A kite fitted with LEDs

  • Some people on social media say this is a kite fitted with red, green and blue, or RGB, lights. Since it is an urban area, people may fly such kites for entertainment.
  • However, some users say it would be difficult to fly such a kite amid wartime conditions. This is a security issue, and the Iranian military has prohibited such activities.

A glowing object was also reportedly seen over the Iranian city of Mashhad on the night of 19 September, but this could not be confirmed.

3. Fake video generated by AI

  • After analysing the video, Elon Musk's company's AI tool Grok said that advanced AI-generated videos can look like real camera footage.
  • However, Grok also acknowledged that this appeared to be real footage recorded on a phone.
  • The video also attracted attention because exactly 50 years ago, on 19 September, similarly strange, colourful objects were seen flying in Iran.

What was seen in Iran 50 years ago?

The incident that took place in Tehran on the night of 19 September 1976 is one of the most extensively studied UFO cases in the world.

According to a report by the US Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA),

  • Around midnight, at least four civilians in Tehran's Shemiran area saw a bright object in the sky and alerted the nearby Mehrabad Airport air traffic control tower (ATC).
  • ATC air traffic controller Hossein Pirouzi also saw the object on the radar. He said it was rectangular, with two large lights at either end and a red light spinning in circles in the middle.
  • Pirouzi informed Iranian Air Force General Yousefi about it. Yousefi had also seen it from his balcony. He sent an 'F-4 Phantom II' fighter aircraft to intercept it.

Iran's F-4 Phantom II aircraft can fly at an altitude of up to 60,000 feet.

  • According to Lieutenant Yaddi Nazeri, who was aboard the jet, when they came within about 46 km of the object, the jet's navigation, communication and weapons systems suddenly shut down. They then returned to base, where all the systems began working again.
  • Nazeri later said that the object was moving away much faster than his jet. His jet was travelling at twice the speed of sound, or Mach 2. He became convinced that he had encountered a UFO from beyond Earth.
  • Ten minutes later, pilot Major Parvez Jafri took off in the second Phantom jet. He spotted it on the jet's radar, rapidly moving away at a distance of around 50 km.
  • Jafri said the object was about the size of a large Boeing 707 aircraft. It was emitting such bright red, green, orange and blue lights that its structure could not be made out clearly.
  • Jafri later said, "A round object emerged from it and began coming straight towards me like a missile, but as soon as I tried to fire a missile at it, my weapon control panel and communication system stopped working."
  • Jafri had to turn his jet to defend himself. The object later moved away. Jafri was ordered to return.
  • On the way back, Jafari saw the diamond-shaped object to his left. Something bright emerged from it and descended directly towards the ground, landing in a dry lake. The next day, Jafari went there by helicopter to look for it, but found nothing. However, people living in nearby homes said they had seen a flash accompanied by a loud sound the previous night.
  • According to former Iranian Air Force Lieutenant Commander Shapur Azarbarzin, the object was travelling at up to Mach 3. At that time, only a few fighter jets from the US and Russia could fly at that speed.

Relations between the US and Iran were good at the time. A report on the incident was submitted to the US Air Force. The US and several institutions in Europe investigated the incident, but to this day it has not been established whether it was an alien UFO, a meteorite, a shooting star or a foreign aircraft.

Are new weapons also tested under the guise of aliens?

New weapons are not tested under the guise of aliens, but there have been several occasions when people mistook a new military aircraft for an alien UFO. Governments, too, did not reveal the truth behind it.

Area 51 is a desert region in the US state of Nevada. It is a highly secure military testing site where several new aircraft have been secretly tested.

According to a secret document of the US intelligence agency CIA obtained by George Washington University in 2013, Area 51 was specifically chosen in 1955 for the secret testing of the U-2 spy aircraft. It could fly at a much higher altitude than many other aircraft of that time.

Commercial aircraft flew at around 20,000 feet and military aircraft at around 40,000 feet, but the U-2 could fly at 60,000 feet or even higher. At that altitude, sunlight fell on its wings while it was already dark below. This made it look bright and strangely shaped.

More than half of the UFO reports recorded in the 1950s and 1960s were actually caused by the U-2 aircraft's secret flights. The programmes were top secret, so the Air Force could not tell the public the truth. People began to believe they were UFOs.

The US' Lockheed U-2 spy plane.

Besides the U-2, test flights of the A-12 spy plane were also conducted at Area 51. Its shiny titanium body and raised central section looked like a 'flying saucer', and people continued to mistake it for a UFO.

In 1981, the F-117 Nighthawk stealth fighter jet also flew here for the first time. Its unusual, triangular design made it look like an alien aircraft to people.

When a country tests new military technology in complete secrecy, its unfamiliar shape, lights or unexpected flight patterns can appear to ordinary people like an alien spacecraft.

The video from Tehran attracted even more attention because the Iran-US war is ongoing, and on 19 September, Iranian Army and IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said, "If tensions with the United States escalate, Iran will use new weapons. They will have such power that the world will be astonished. Iran is prepared for a long war."

However, it is not clear whether this is a new Iranian drone, an American one or something else.

So, is there really nothing like aliens and their spaceships?

So far, no government, space agency or scientist has any conclusive evidence of the existence of aliens.

The US organisation AARO, which works on the alien theory, and the US space agency NASA say the same thing: "Despite investigating hundreds of cases, no alien remains or evidence of any extraterrestrial technology has been found."

AARO's report released in November 2024 made 3 key points...

  • Since 2022, AARO has received reports of 1,652 unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UAP - unexplained unusual events.
  • Most of these cases were found to be related to weather, birds, satellites, drones, aircraft, meteors and other such phenomena.
  • However, 21 cases had some unusual features. Investigations into such cases are therefore under way.

AARO Director John Kosloski had said, "Despite my studies in physics and engineering and my experience in intelligence, I have still not been able to understand these intriguing cases. I also do not know anyone who can understand them."

The full details of these 21 'interesting' cases are not public. However, according to John Kosloski, all these incidents occurred around US military bases or other national security-related sites, so they were captured by sensors or radar in addition to eyewitnesses. In most cases, objects shaped like spheres, cylinders or triangles were seen...

  • In 2024, a US officer saw a round orange object resembling a car at an altitude of hundreds of feet. Its red and blue lights illuminated the inside of their car. The object first tilted downwards and then rapidly moved upwards without making a sound.
  • In one case, two people saw a brightly lit, cylinder-shaped object as large as a commercial plane, which disappeared after 15 seconds.
  • In 2013, an aircraft spotted an object flying near an airport in Puerto Rico.

NASA also rejected the theory of aliens in September 2023. However, it also said that there were some cases for which no natural explanation could be found, nor could they be linked to any human activity.
